items.title: 1.6 Assessment of total uncertainty in the final result

source_refs.note: Topic 1.6 with Examples 1.1 to 1.3 and the thumb-rule, colour-printing and light-travel side boxes (PDF 12-14, printed 9-11).

blocks.text: Knowing the uncertainties in all the factors involved in a calculation, the maximum possible uncertainty or error in the final result can be found as follows.

Absolute uncertainties are added. For example, the distance between two positions x1 = 15.4 +/- 0.1 cm and x2 = 25.6 +/- 0.1 cm is recorded as x = x2 - x1 = 10.2 +/- 0.2 cm, and the addition of two lengths l1 = 8.5 +/- 0.1 cm and l2 = 12.6 +/- 0.1 cm is recorded as l = l1 + l2 = 21.1 +/- 0.2 cm.

Percentage uncertainties are added. For example, the maximum possible uncertainty in the value of the resistance R of a conductor, determined from the potential difference V applied across it and the resulting current I, is estimated as follows. Let V = 3.4 +/- 0.1 V and I = 0.68 +/- 0.05 A, using R = V/I. The percentage uncertainty in V is (0.1 V / 3.4 V) x 100 = 3%, and in I it is (0.05 A / 0.68 A) x 100 = 7%. Hence the total percentage uncertainty in R is 3 + 7 = 10%. The value of R is R = 3.4 V / 0.68 A = 5.0 ohm, written as R = 5.0 +/- 0.5 ohm; the uncertainty, being an estimate only, is recorded to one significant figure.

The percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power factor in the formula. For example, in calculating the cross-sectional area of a cylinder of radius r = 1.25 cm from A = pi r^2, the percentage uncertainty in A is 2 x the percentage uncertainty in r. Because the uncertainty is multiplied by the power factor, it increases the precision demand of the measurement. When the radius of a small sphere is measured as 1.25 cm by Vernier callipers with least count 0.01 cm, the radius is recorded as r = 1.25 +/- 0.01 cm; the percentage uncertainty in r is (0.01 / 1.25) x 100 = 0.8%; the total percentage uncertainty in A is 2 x 0.8 = 1.6%; thus A = pi r^2 = 3.14 x (1.25)^2 = 4.906 with 1.6% uncertainty, and the result should be recorded as A = 4.91 +/- 0.08 cm^2.

blocks.title: Example 1.1
blocks.text: The length, breadth and thickness of a metal sheet are 2.03 m, 1.22 m and 0.95 cm. Volume V = l x b x h = 2.03 m x 1.22 m x 0.95 x 10^-2 m = 2.35277 x 10^-2 m^3. As the factor 0.95 cm has the minimum number of significant figures, two, the volume is recorded to two significant figures: V = 2.4 x 10^-2 m^3.

blocks.title: Example 1.2
blocks.text: The mass of a metal box measured by a lever balance is 3.25 kg; two silver coins of masses 10.01 g and 10.02 g measured by a beam balance are added to it. Total mass = 3.25 kg + 0.01001 kg + 0.01002 kg = 3.27003 kg. Since the least precise mass, 3.25 kg, has two decimal places, the total mass is reported to two decimal places: total mass = 3.27 kg.

blocks.title: Example 1.3
blocks.text: The diameter and length of a metal cylinder measured with Vernier callipers of least count 0.01 cm are 1.25 cm and 3.35 cm. Absolute uncertainty in length = 0.01 cm, percentage uncertainty in length = (0.01 cm / 3.35 cm) x 100 = 0.3%; absolute uncertainty in diameter = 0.01 cm, percentage uncertainty in diameter = (0.01 cm / 1.25 cm) x 100 = 0.8%. Volume V = pi r^2 l = pi (d^2 / 4) l, so the total uncertainty in V = 2 x (%age uncertainty in diameter) + (%age uncertainty in length) = 2 x 0.8 + 0.3 = 1.9%. V = 3.14 x (1.25 cm)^2 x 3.35 cm / 4 = 4.1089842 cm^3 with 1.9% uncertainty, thus V = (4.11 +/- 0.08) cm^3, where 4.11 cm^3 is the calculated volume and 0.08 the uncertainty in it.

Colour printing uses just four colours, cyan, magenta, yellow and black, to produce the entire range of colours in this book. The travel time of light is 1 min 20 s from the Moon to the Earth, 8 min 20 s from the Sun, and 5 h 20 s from Pluto.
